Then reason: wave speed u = 10 cm/s = 0.10 m/s, wavelength λ = 0.5 m, amplitude A = 10 cm = 0.10 m. raw_record.question_text:
A transverse sinusoidal wave moves along a string in the positive $x$-direction at a speed of 10 cm/s. The wavelength of the wave is 0.5 m and its amplitude is 10 cm. At a particular time $t$, the snapshot of the wave is shown in the figure. What is the velocity of point P when its displacement is 5 cm?
<image_1>

method.method_draft: First read the figure: the axes are x horizontal to the right and y vertical upward; point P is on the positive-displacement part of the sinusoid, on the descending branch after a crest, so the local slope at P is negative. From the text read wave speed u = 10 cm/s = 0.10 m/s, wavelength lambda = 0.5 m, amplitude A = 10 cm = 0.10 m, and the requested displacement y = 5 cm = 0.05 m. Treat each point of the string as executing SHM with angular frequency omega = 2 pi u / lambda = 0.4 pi rad/s. At displacement y, the transverse speed magnitude is omega sqrt(A^2 - y^2). Use the figure only to determine the sign: since the wave travels in +x and P lies on a negative-slope segment, the transverse velocity is upward. Thus compute omega sqrt(0.10^2 - 0.05^2) and attach +j direction.
